scope: Every step of the companion-backed (01) archive and scan inspection. The eight unchanged legacy pipelines in this category do not yet have companions and are outside this manifest. Step indices are zero-based.

filters.purpose: Inspect measured Slice_1.ang directly before archiving all 117 raw sections. The imported 189 by 201 grid has 0.25 micrometer XY spacing; the reader gives its single Z layer a 1 micrometer placeholder spacing.

Preserve acquisition-frame Euler radians before the in-place frame rotation. The subsequent sample rotation reorders this copy with every other cell array; values retain their acquisition-frame meaning.
Apply the established SmallIN100 EDAX/TSL Euler reference-frame correction: 90 degrees about Z. EulerAngles are radians and are modified in place; this does not rearrange image cells.

Apply the established 180 degree Y sample reference-frame correction slice by slice. Corrected orientation values and cell ordering agree with Read H5EBSD using recommended transforms, but geometry origins differ. Retain this inspection's transform-derived origin; do not overlay it on archive readback without checking alignment. Imported X/Y Position remain acquisition-coordinate attributes.

Use the existing SmallIN100 admission rule: Image Quality > 120 AND Confidence Index > 0.1. Read ANG remaps phase zero to one, so Phases > 0 would wrongly accept failed indexing. Keep rejected cells but exclude them from colors.

Color accepted measurements by crystal direction parallel to corrected sample Z using the native IPF color key. Black marks rejected cells, not a second phase; color differences are not a scalar misorientation measure.
Save the single-scan inspection checkpoint separately from the raw stack archive. This is a 2D map with placeholder Z thickness, not a reconstructed 3D volume.

Archive all 117 original ANG sections using the unchanged EDAX preset, high-to-low stack order and 0.25 micrometer section pitch; raw data and frame metadata are written independently of the inspection arrays.
